jobs.title: Senior Business Development Representative
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Kestra

Kestra has delivered exceptional commercial results through a strong inbound business motion. Now is the time to add a complementary outbound motion by leveraging the open source adoption signals we already have, engaging directly with open source developers and engineering stakeholders, and encouraging them to explore our Enterprise and Cloud products.

In March 2026, we closed a $25M Series A led by RTP Global, with participation from Alven, ISAI, and Axeleo – backed by founders from Datadog, dbt Labs, and Hugging Face.

The role

We are looking for a technically curious, open source driven, autonomous Senior BDR who will build the first outbound motion at Kestra. You will work from open source signals, understand real world usage, and create the bridge that encourages developers and engineers to explore Enterprise and Cloud offerings at the right moment.

Your mission

  • Open strategic conversations through outbound, powered by open source intent

  • Understand how developers use plugins, blueprints, and workflows, and capture high signal context

  • Engage confidently with engineering and open source contributors, speaking their language with credibility

  • Encourage exploration of Kestra Enterprise and Kestra Cloud through outcome driven narratives

  • Build repeatable research, qualification, and outreach standards

  • Experiment, iterate, and shape the first outbound motion with autonomy and speed

  • Generate SQL pipeline that converts signal into enterprise adoption

  • Help define the future of orchestration GTM

Who you are

  • Curious technically, comfortable understanding open source usage patterns

  • You enjoy automation and orchestration markets and know the landscape

  • You like open source, you are curious, you explore, you test, you learn fast

  • You use AI tools for business research, outreach, and signal based prospecting

  • You are autonomous, proactive, and you think like a builder

  • You are fast in execution, structured in approach, human in communication

  • You prefer creating motions to following scripts

  • You want to build something that scales, early, and make an impact

What you get

  • Build the first outbound BDR engine in a category defining open source orchestration platform

  • Freedom to experiment and iterate on GTM motion

  • Product proximity and exposure to strategy, roadmap influence, and market narratives

  • A product used for mission critical workloads, not demos

  • Competitive fixed salary, strong OTE, equity, health insurance, and essential benefits

jobs.title: Senior Field Engineer, France
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Senior / Principal · Remote in France · CDI

Be our first Field Engineer in France, joining a global field engineering team in Europe, US and India. Help major enterprises adopt Kestra, from the first technical conversation through production and expansion, and shape how we build Field Engineering in France.

You may know this role as Solutions Engineer, Solutions Architect or Pre-Sales Engineer.

Reporting to: Lead Field Engineer
Languages: Fluent French and English
Location: Anywhere in France, with customer visits when needed

Why Kestra

Orchestrate everything, everywhere. From one control plane.

Data, infrastructure, business processes and AI agents. Build, run and govern them all, in the cloud or on your own servers. AI agents follow the same rules as everything else.

We believe orchestration is becoming a shared layer of enterprise architecture: the layer that coordinates what runs across tools, teams and environments. Enterprises have accumulated isolated pockets of automation, each with its own rules and a partial view of dependencies. Hybrid cloud and AI agents make the need for a common foundation more urgent.

Kestra is building that foundation as an open-source platform. For enterprises, unified orchestration means less fragmented automation, consistent governance and the ability to introduce new use cases without rebuilding execution and control mechanisms each time.

Founded in France, we are growing our enterprise business in both France and the United States. In March 2026, we raised a $25M Series A led by RTP Global, with Alven, ISAI and Axeleo. Teams at JPMorgan Chase, Apple, TotalEnergies, Crédit Agricole, Leroy Merlin, Bloomberg and T-Systems run Kestra in production.

The opportunity

Our French customers include banks, insurers, industrial groups, energy companies and retailers. Their projects involve critical systems, complex migrations and demanding architecture reviews.

You will be the technical partner who helps them evaluate Kestra, make sound architectural decisions and reach production. You will stay involved as adoption grows, seeing the results of the choices you helped them make.

You will work directly with Product and Engineering, inspect the open-source code, and help shape what we build next. As our first Field Engineer in France, you will also establish methods and reference architectures that future colleagues can build on.

This is a senior individual contributor role, with level and scope matched to your experience.

What you will do

  • Lead technical evaluations with the Account Executive. Understand the customer's environment, agree on use cases and success criteria, build demos and proofs of concept, and design the target architecture.

  • Help customers reach production. Guide onboarding, train teams and review migration plans so customers can operate Kestra confidently.

  • Grow adoption within your accounts. Identify new teams and workloads with your Account Executive, building on your understanding of the customer's systems.

  • Help resolve difficult issues. Work with Support and Engineering on investigations, bringing customer context and clear communication.

  • Turn field experience into better products and practices. Give Product concrete feedback, create reusable blueprints and migration guides, and share useful knowledge with the open-source community.

What you bring

  • Enterprise customer experience. You have independently led technical evaluations or architecture workshops and can challenge and advise experienced technical leaders.

  • Hands-on engineering ability. You write and debug code, troubleshoot deployments and investigate failures across applications, infrastructure and networks.

  • Production orchestration experience. You have operated, integrated or replaced an orchestrator or a substantial automation setup that other teams depend on.

  • Depth in data engineering, platform engineering / infrastructure automation, or AI / MLOps. You bring expertise in one area and can learn across the others.

  • Ownership and communication. You can take an ambiguous project to a working outcome and explain your decisions clearly in French and English.

The work involves Kubernetes, Docker, YAML, Git, CI/CD, Terraform or OpenTofu, and enterprise security requirements. Depending on the account, you may encounter Python, SQL, dbt, Spark or Kafka, and migrations from Control-M, Automic, VMware vRA / Aria, Airflow or similar systems.

Your background may be in a vendor, consultancy, startup or enterprise platform team. We care about the work you have owned and the judgment you bring.

At Principal level, we also look for impact beyond your own projects: mentoring engineers, setting architectural direction or creating methods others adopt.

The demanding parts

Enterprise migrations take patience. Security reviews, legacy constraints and internal decisions can slow progress, and some evaluations will be lost for reasons outside your control.

Customers will expect clear thinking during difficult incidents. You will also balance their immediate needs with building reusable approaches for the team. Part of the playbook will be yours to write.

What we offer

  • Compensation benchmarked against US software vendors hiring for comparable roles in France, discussed in the first conversation.

  • BSPCE equity participation.

  • Remote work across France, with flexibility around customer and team commitments.

  • An annual company offsite.

  • Equipment, conference and training budgets, with time to learn.

How we hire

  1. 45 minutes with our Lead Field Engineer: your experience, a real architecture or project discussed in depth, and your questions.

  2. 45 minutes with Emmanuel, our CEO: Kestra's direction, your ambitions and how we would work together.

Two conversations, no take-home exercise, and a decision within a week of the first call.

Send your CV or LinkedIn profile.

jobs.title: Account Executive
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Kestra

Kestra is the universal orchestration platform — open source, declarative, and designed to orchestrate data pipelines, IT automation, business workflows, and AI/agentic systems.

Trusted by over 10,000 organizations worldwide — including JPMorgan Chase, Bloomberg, FILA, and Crédit Agricole — Kestra orchestrates mission-critical workloads at scale. The open-source project has close to 30,000 GitHub stars, hundreds of contributors, and a fast-growing global community.

In March 2026, we closed a $25M Series A led by RTP Global, with participation from Alven, ISAI, and Axeleo – backed by founders from Datadog, dbt Labs, and Hugging Face.

The Role

We're looking for an Account Executive based in Germany to drive enterprise sales across the DACH region. You'll own the full sales cycle for Kestra's Enterprise Edition, from prospecting and qualification through negotiation and close.

This is a fully remote position. Because the role requires regular engagement with German-speaking enterprise buyers, we're hiring specifically from Germany.

What You'll Do

  • Own the full sales cycle for enterprise accounts in the DACH region, from outbound prospecting to contract close.

  • Build and manage a qualified pipeline through a mix of outbound efforts, inbound leads, and community-sourced opportunities from Kestra's open-source user base.

  • Run discovery calls, product demos (in partnership with Solution Engineers), and commercial negotiations with technical and business stakeholders.

  • Develop account strategies for target organizations, mapping decision-makers across engineering, data, and IT leadership.

  • Collaborate closely with Solution Engineers, Developer Advocates, and Product to align messaging with what Kestra delivers in practice.

  • Provide accurate pipeline forecasts and maintain disciplined CRM hygiene.

What We're Looking For

  • Proven track record in B2B enterprise software sales, ideally selling to technical buyers (engineering leaders, platform teams, data teams).

  • Experience selling in the DACH market with an existing network of enterprise contacts being a strong advantage.

  • Ability to understand technical products at a level that earns credibility with engineering stakeholders. You don't need to write code, but you need to follow a technical conversation about infrastructure, orchestration, or automation.

  • Fluent in both English and German (written and spoken) at a professional level.

  • Comfortable operating in a startup environment with minimal structure. You build your own playbook rather than waiting for one.

  • Strong communicator who can translate technical capabilities into business value for different audiences.

Bonus Points

  • Experience selling open-source or developer-focused products where community adoption drives commercial conversion.

  • Familiarity with orchestration, workflow automation, data engineering, or infrastructure tooling.

  • Past experience at a B2B SaaS company, especially in an early-stage or growth-stage environment.

  • Understanding of land-and-expand sales motions and usage-based pricing models.

What You Get

  • Real ownership in a globally distributed, technical team.

  • Direct exposure to product strategy and company priorities.

  • A product used for mission-critical workloads — not demos.

  • Competitive compensation, equity, and health insurance.

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Location: Remote (US East Coast)


About Kestra

Kestra is the universal orchestration platform — open source, API-first, and built to orchestrate everything: data pipelines, IT automation, business workflows, and AI/agentic systems.

Close to 30,000 GitHub stars. Over 10,000 organizations running Kestra worldwide. Mission-critical workloads at JPMorgan Chase, Bloomberg, Apple, and Crédit Agricole. Two billion workflows executed in 2025 alone.

We just closed a $25M Series A led by RTP Global ($36M total raised). We're building the Orchestration Control Plane of the AI Era — and we need someone on the ground in the US to turn open-source traction into enterprise revenue.

The Role

This is a hunter role. You'll own the full enterprise sales cycle on the US East Coast — from sourcing and qualifying opportunities to running complex, multi-stakeholder deals through to close. Your territory covers some of the largest financial services, healthcare, and technology organizations in the world.

You won't be handed a playbook. You'll build one. This is our first dedicated enterprise AE in the region, and we need someone who thrives in that kind of environment — high autonomy, direct access to founders, and real impact on how we go to market in the US.

A significant part of your pipeline will come from Kestra's open-source community: engineering teams already using the product in production. You'll turn that organic adoption into commercial relationships at the enterprise level.

What You'll Do

  • Own the full sales cycle for enterprise accounts on the US East Coast, from first touch to signed contract. Typical deal sizes: $50K–$500K+ ARR.

  • Build pipeline through a mix of outbound prospecting, inbound leads, partner referrals, and community-sourced opportunities from Kestra's open-source user base.

  • Run discovery and demos in partnership with Solution Engineers. Lead commercial negotiations with both technical and business stakeholders — VPs of Engineering, Heads of Data, Platform leads, and occasionally C-suite.

  • Develop account strategies for target organizations: map buying committees, identify champions, understand procurement workflows, and navigate complex enterprise decision-making.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Solution Engineers, Developer Advocates, Marketing, and Product to sharpen messaging, surface product feedback, and align on what Kestra delivers in practice.

  • Maintain forecasting discipline. Accurate pipeline reporting, clean CRM, no surprises.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of B2B enterprise software sales experience, closing deals in the $50K–$500K+ range with complex buying committees.

  • Proven quota attainment. You've been a top performer — top 10-20% of your sales org — and can show a consistent track record of hitting or exceeding targets.

  • Experience selling to technical buyers: engineering leaders, platform teams, data teams, DevOps/infrastructure teams. You earn credibility in technical conversations. You don't need to write YAML, but you need to understand why someone would.

  • Hunter DNA. You've built pipeline from scratch, not just worked inbound. Outbound prospecting is part of how you operate, not something you tolerate.

  • Comfortable in a startup environment with minimal structure. You build your own playbook, define your own territory strategy, and move fast without waiting for permission.

  • Strong communicator who can translate deep technical capabilities into business value for different audiences — from a Staff Engineer evaluating orchestration tools to a VP making a platform bet.

Bonus Points

  • Experience selling open-source or developer-focused products where community adoption drives commercial conversion (PLG/open-core models).

  • Familiarity with orchestration, workflow automation, data engineering, or infrastructure tooling — you understand the ecosystem Kestra competes in.

  • Past experience at a Series A–C stage company where you helped define and scale the sales motion.

  • Understanding of land-and-expand sales strategies and usage-based or consumption-based pricing models.

  • Existing network of enterprise contacts in financial services, healthcare, or technology on the US East Coast.

What You Get

  • Real ownership in a globally distributed, high-caliber technical team. This isn't a cog-in-the-machine role.

  • Direct access to founders and influence on product strategy, go-to-market approach, and company priorities.

  • A product that sells itself — Kestra is already running mission-critical workloads at Fortune 500 companies. You're not selling vaporware.

  • Competitive compensation: strong base + uncapped commission + equity.

  • Health insurance, flexible PTO, and remote-first culture.

jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer

postalAddress.streetAddress: Le Neo 2, 12 Rue Denis Papin Bâtiment A

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Kestra

Kestra is the universal orchestration platform: open source, declarative, and designed to orchestrate data pipelines, IT automation, business workflows, and AI/agentic systems.

Trusted by over 10,000 organizations worldwide, including JPMorgan Chase, Bloomberg, FILA, and Crédit Agricole, Kestra orchestrates mission-critical workloads at scale. The open-source project has close to 30,000 GitHub stars, hundreds of contributors, and a fast-growing global community.

About the role

Kestra runs arbitrary, user-defined code at scale. Our users write workflows that execute scripts, containers, and queries against their own production systems, through hundreds of community-built plugins, on a platform whose entire source code is public. That is an unusually rich attack surface, and securing it is a genuinely hard engineering problem rather than a checklist exercise.
You would be our first dedicated security hire. We're looking for a Senior Security Engineer to own and elevate the end-to-end security posture of our platform, infrastructure, and open-source ecosystem.
This is a unique, hybrid role for someone who excels at both sides of security: actively breaking systems to find vulnerabilities (hands-on penetration testing) and actively fixing them (opening PRs, patching infrastructure, and managing supply chain risks). If you want to build a world-class security foundation for a fast-growing open-source and SaaS platform, this role is for you.
This is a hands-on engineering role, not a GRC or compliance one.

What you would do

Your first six months would focus on the first three points below. The rest is where the role grows.

  • Conduct hands-on penetration testing and threat modeling across our web application, APIs, control plane, and cloud environments.

  • Manage end-to-end vulnerability tracking across our codebases, software dependencies (SCA), container images, and cloud infrastructure.

  • Proactively fix security flaws by writing patches, submitting Pull Requests (PRs), or collaborating directly with product teams to guide remediation.

  • Audit and harden our cloud infrastructure (GCP, Kubernetes clusters, and networking configurations) against external and internal threats.

  • Automate security tooling into our CI/CD pipelines (SAST, DAST, dependency scanners) to catch CVEs before code reaches production.

  • Perform security code reviews and evaluate third-party dependencies, open-source integrations, and supply-chain risks.

  • Lead incident response efforts and establish continuous monitoring, detection, and mitigation strategies.

  • Own our public security posture as an open-source project: vulnerability disclosure process, CVE handling, security advisories, and the trust model of our plugin ecosystem.

Our Tech Stack

  • Security & Vulnerability Tools: Trivy, GitHub Security / Dependabot, Elastic Security

  • Infrastructure: Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform

  • Cloud: GCP

  • Programming language: Java, Typescript, Javascript

  • Datastore: PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch

  • Queuing: Redis, Kafka, AMQP

  • Monitoring & Logs: ELK, Prometheus, Grafana

  • Deployment & Repository: GitHub Actions, ArgoCD

What we are looking for

  • 5+ years of experience in Security Engineering, Product Security, DevSecOps, or a combined Offensive/Defensive role.

  • Strong hands-on penetration testing background, with proven ability to discover application, API, and network-level vulnerabilities.

  • A builder/fixer mindset: You don't just export scanner PDFs; you can read code, understand exploits, write fixes, or provide clear remediation steps to engineers.

  • Deep familiarity with cloud security (AWS or GCP) and containerized environments (Kubernetes, Docker).

  • Experience with dependency and supply-chain security (CVE management, open-source licensing, SCA tools).

  • Fluent in English and comfortable working autonomously in a fully remote environment.

  • Adaptability to a fast-paced open-source startup environment where pragmatism and execution speed matter.

Perks & Benefits

  • Work from anywhere: We’re a remote-first company, so you can work from wherever feels like home. Plus, you’ll have access to coworking spaces worldwide if you ever need a change of scenery.

  • Health coverage: From medical support, dental, and vision, we've got you covered.

  • Home office setup on us: We’ll provide all the equipment you need to work comfortably.

     

Our Hiring Process

We aim to move quickly (2-3 weeks), but we can adjust the timeline if needed.

  • Intro call with the hiring manager (30 min)

  • Technical scenario / Practical assessment (2 hours, asynchronous homework focusing on threat assessment and remediation)

  • Team chat with one of your future colleagues (30 min)

  • Final discussion with one of our co-founders (30 min)

ABOUT THE ROLE

Kestra runs arbitrary, user-defined code at scale. Our users write workflows that execute scripts, containers, and queries against their own production systems, through hundreds of community-built plugins, on a platform whose entire source code is public. That is an unusually rich attack surface, and securing it is a genuinely hard engineering problem rather than a checklist exercise.
You would be our first dedicated security hire. We're looking for a Senior Security Engineer to own and elevate the end-to-end security posture of our platform, infrastructure, and open-source ecosystem.
This is a unique, hybrid role for someone who excels at both sides of security: actively breaking systems to find vulnerabilities (hands-on penetration testing) and actively fixing them (opening PRs, patching infrastructure, and managing supply chain risks). If you want to build a world-class security foundation for a fast-growing open-source and SaaS platform, this role is for you.
This is a hands-on engineering role, not a GRC or compliance one.

 - Infrastructure: Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform

 - Cloud: GCP

 - Programming language: Java, Typescript, Javascript

 - Datastore: PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch

 - Queuing: Redis, Kafka, AMQP

 - Monitoring & Logs: ELK, Prometheus, Grafana

 - A builder/fixer mindset: You don't just export scanner PDFs; you can read code, understand exploits, write fixes, or provide clear remediation steps to engineers.

 - Deep familiarity with cloud security (AWS or GCP) and containerized environments (Kubernetes, Docker).

 - Experience with dependency and supply-chain security (CVE management, open-source licensing, SCA tools).

 - Adaptability to a fast-paced open-source startup environment where pragmatism and execution speed matter.

jobs.title: Senior Demand Generation Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Kestra

Kestra is a unified orchestration platform. One engine runs data pipelines, infrastructure operations, the scheduled scripts scattered across a company that nobody wants to touch, business processes that pause for a human decision, and now agents choosing their next move — all as executions in the same place, with one history to search when something breaks and one set of rules deciding who may run what.

More than four billion workflows a year run on Kestra, and more than ten Fortune 500 companies are customers. The open-source project has more than 27,000 GitHub stars and 2,000+ plugins, and the engine, interface, editor, and plugins stay open source under Apache 2.0.

In March 2026, we closed a $25M Series A led by RTP Global, with participation from Alven, ISAI, and Axeleo. Enterprises run Kestra in production because it delivers what legacy schedulers and point automation tools can't: unified governance, hybrid execution, and engineering-grade reliability.

The Role

Kestra is hiring a Senior Demand Generation Manager to own the program layer that turns product and market signals into enterprise pipeline.

You own the demand-generation plan, the multi-channel programs, and marketing’s contribution to the enterprise pipeline, with shared accountability alongside Sales. You translate Kestra's go-to-market strategy into campaigns that create and progress qualified enterprise opportunities.

This is a senior individual contributor role reporting to the Head of Marketing. You partner closely with Sales, Product Marketing, Developer Advocacy, and Growth Engineering.

Growth Engineering owns the outbound automation engine, data enrichment, and attribution instrumentation, and hands you a signal layer built from product usage, community activity, web and GitHub activity, and enrichment data. You take that layer and build the named target-account list and the programs that turn it into enterprise pipeline. You are not building that infrastructure and you are not maintaining it. We don't buy, we build, and this role is for a marketer who works the same way: automating and experimenting on modern, AI-native tooling.

You'll join a small, senior enterprise marketing team where each person owns a function rather than a product line: this role owns demand and campaigns, a peer owns positioning and competitive, another owns customer evidence and content, and another owns technical proof and demos.

Kestra's advantage is converting one of the strongest open-source communities in orchestration into enterprise pipeline. That motion doesn't look like standard top-down demand generation, and you'll help define it.

What You'll Own

The demand plan and the number

  • Build and own the demand-generation plan against Kestra's enterprise go-to-market strategy, establishing program and pipeline targets in partnership with the Head of Marketing and Sales.

  • Build Kestra's enterprise account-tiering model, translating product, community, and firmographic signals into target segments and account priorities, and align with Sales on the accounts that matter most.

  • Bring today’s outbound campaigns under one coordinated demand strategy, so programs running across Marketing, Growth Engineering, and Business Development share target accounts, a common thesis, and measurable outcomes.

  • Partner with Growth Engineering to identify open-source deployments showing production-scale, multi-user, enterprise-shaped usage, and build the programs that turn those signals into enterprise conversations.

  • Build multi-threaded account programs that engage multiple members of the buying group across technical, operational, and economic roles, moving accounts from initial technical interest toward qualified enterprise opportunities.

Multi-channel programs

  • Design and run integrated campaigns across paid media, content, email, webinars, and events, coordinated toward pipeline rather than run as one-offs.

  • Build and run paid acquisition directly in the platforms. You will be hands-on in LinkedIn Ads and Google Ads, owning targeting, creative testing, and spend pacing. This is a lean budget you are expected to make work, not an agency retainer you supervise.

  • Shape account-based and competitive-displacement strategy for market-shift moments, briefing the outbound automation engine and wrapping it with multi-channel air cover.

  • Own the program execution behind our flagship legacy-displacement campaign: targeting, channels, sequencing, budget, and cadence. Product Marketing owns the campaign brief and customer proof; you own how the program reaches and progresses target accounts, against a shared pipeline number.

  • Own the campaign assets that carry your programs: landing pages, nurture copy, and conversion paths. Content marketing and customer evidence sit with a peer — you brief them, they supply the story.

  • Coordinate with business development on contact-level outreach so account-level programs and individual outreach reinforce each other.

Nurture and conversion

  • Build the nurture and lifecycle programs that move prospects and self-serve users toward enterprise conversations.

  • Improve conversion across the funnel, from first touch to qualified opportunity.

Measurement

  • We measure at the account level, not the lead level. A qualified account means at least three people across two or more buying roles engaged within a defined window. If your instinct is to drive MQL volume, this role will frustrate you.

  • Instrument every program so you can tie its contribution to pipeline, working from the attribution and data foundation Growth Engineering maintains.

  • Report in the terms the business runs on — qualified accounts created, pipeline generated and progressed, and program efficiency — for quarterly business reviews.

  • Own demand-generation program budget and channel allocation, moving investment toward what is producing pipeline.

  • Manage agencies and partners where they extend your reach.

What We're Looking For

  • Typically 6+ years in demand generation, growth, or account-based marketing in B2B SaaS, with direct ownership of pipeline targets and outcomes.

  • Proven across the demand stack: multi-channel campaigns (paid, content, email, events), lifecycle and nurture, ABM strategy, and the marketing-to-sales handoff.

  • Hands-on paid media experience. You have built and run campaigns yourself in LinkedIn Ads and Google Ads, and you can explain what you changed, why you changed it, and how it affected acquisition efficiency, account engagement, or pipeline.

  • A builder who automates and treats every campaign as an experiment — comfortable partnering with a technical growth-engineering function rather than owning the tooling end to end.

  • Analytically rigorous. You pull your own data, build your own views, and interrogate a pipeline report rather than forward it.

  • You work with AI the way a senior marketer works with a capable junior: brief it, review what comes back, ship what's good, fix what isn't. You verify every claim against a primary source before it reaches a prospect. We are not measuring volume of documents.

  • Familiarity with developer-led, open-source, or product-led motions — or the curiosity and adaptability to master one fast.

  • You operate independently with urgency and ownership in fast-scaling environments where the process is still being defined.

  • Genuine respect for the open-source community. Kestra's open-source users are not a lead list, and the credibility of the open-source project is the foundation the enterprise business is built on. Nothing you build gates or diminishes the free product.

We know strong candidates often hold back unless they match every line. If you meet most of this, we'd like to hear from you.

What Makes This Role Worth Your Time

  • Real ownership from day one: enterprise demand programs, ABM, nurture, and campaign performance, with direct access to leadership and real influence on go-to-market.

  • A signal and enrichment layer already built and maintained for you, drawn from product usage, community activity, web and GitHub activity, and enrichment data. Most companies our size do not have it. You build the target-account list and the programs on top of it.

  • A build-not-buy culture where you're expected to automate and experiment on modern, AI-native tooling.

  • A genuinely differentiated go-to-market: converting one of the strongest open-source communities in orchestration into enterprise revenue.

  • A platform in production at enterprises that cannot afford downtime.

  • A senior IC seat that stays one. Scope grows with the company, and at our size we are not building management layers.

Compensation and Benefits

  • Competitive compensation, performance bonus, and equity

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Employer-paid life and disability insurance

  • 401(k)

  • Fully remote, with home-office and equipment budget

  • Learning and conference budget

  • Paid time off, company holidays, and parental leave

Location

United States — Remote, with overlap with European working hours, as Product, Engineering, and the founders are based in Europe. Some travel to customer and industry events and company off-sites.

A Note on AI in Our Hiring Process

We use AI-assisted tools to help prepare for candidate conversations. They do not screen applications or make hiring decisions. Every decision about your candidacy is made by a person.

Equal Opportunity

Kestra is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to an inclusive environment for everyone, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

jobs.title: People & Talent Lead

postalAddress.streetAddress: Le Neo 2, 12 Rue Denis Papin Bâtiment A

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Remote from France or Germany · Full-time

Become Kestra’s first dedicated People hire. Help us grow from 50 to 100 people over the next 12 to 18 months, and strengthen the foundations that help a distributed team work well together.

You will own recruitment and People operations, working directly with the founders and hiring managers. This is a hands-on role with room to shape the function as we grow.

Reporting to: Emmanuel (CEO) and Ludovic (CTO), our co-founders
Working language: English

Why Kestra

Orchestrate everything, everywhere. From one control plane.

Data, infrastructure, business processes and AI agents. Build, run and govern them all, in the cloud or on your own servers. AI agents follow the same rules as everything else.

We believe orchestration is becoming a shared layer of enterprise architecture: the layer that coordinates what runs across tools, teams and environments. Kestra is building that foundation as an open-source platform, giving enterprises a common way to manage increasingly complex automation.

Founded in France, we are growing our enterprise business in Europe and the United States. In March 2026, we raised a $25M Series A led by RTP Global, with Alven, ISAI and Axeleo. Teams at JPMorgan Chase, Apple, TotalEnergies, Crédit Agricole, Leroy Merlin, Bloomberg and Deutsche Telekom run Kestra in production.

The opportunity

Our next stage depends on bringing in the right people and helping them succeed. We are hiring across Sales, Engineering, Product, Marketing and Customer Operations, with substantial growth planned across functions and all the regions where we operate.

You will bring dedicated People and Talent leadership to an established organisation, working with the founders, hiring managers and the Administration, Workplace Operations and Finance teams that already support our People processes.

With colleagues across more than ten countries and many recent joiners, the work goes beyond hiring. People need a good start, clear expectations and connections across teams. You will help make that experience consistent as we grow.

What you will own

  • Recruitment from sourcing to signed offer. Find and engage candidates, run initial conversations, coordinate focused interview processes and keep the ATS reliable. Work with the founders and leaders across functions to prioritise roles and help hiring managers make well-supported decisions.

  • People operations across countries. Work with our Administration, Workplace Operations and Finance teams to coordinate contracts, payroll partners, EOR providers, benefits, time off and employee requests. Keep records and deadlines clear, and work with local providers and advisers on employment requirements.

  • Onboarding that gets people started well. Make the practical setup smooth and help managers give new joiners clear expectations, useful context and the right relationships from day one.

  • Compensation and performance processes. Develop the framework with the founders, then run the cycles: salary reviews, levels, performance reviews and equity administration, including BSPCE where applicable.

  • How we work as a distributed team. Organise all-hands and the company offsite, strengthen internal communication and build routines that help people collaborate across locations.

  • A clear view of progress. Give the founders useful information on hiring, headcount and employment costs. Use it to identify bottlenecks and decide what needs attention.

What you bring

  • Experience combining People and Talent in a growing company. You have worked through a period of significant hiring and know which processes become necessary as a team grows.

  • Recruitment experience you have built yourself. You have sourced candidates, assessed them with hiring managers and closed offers. You can explain the difficult searches, the hires that worked and what you learned from those that did not.

  • Experience recruiting across functions. You have hired technical and business profiles, understand how to adapt your approach to different roles and markets, and work with managers to assess evidence of performance beyond a convincing interview.

  • Practical knowledge of international employment. You have worked with EOR providers, payroll partners and local advisers, and know when a situation needs specialist input.

  • Strong operational judgment. You are comfortable in an ATS, HRIS and payroll platforms, handle sensitive information carefully and follow through on details.

  • The ability to build and operate. You can introduce a useful process, run it yourself and improve it without adding unnecessary complexity.

  • Fluent professional English. French or German is useful for working with local employees and providers.

Experience in developer tools or open source, a background in operations or consulting, or experience supporting US employment from Europe would be valuable.

How you will work

You will build on an established organisation, supported by the Administration, Workplace Operations and Finance teams that already carry our People processes. Your role is to bring dedicated expertise, coordinate this work and help it scale as the company grows.

We already use Kestra to automate business and administrative workflows, improving them as our needs evolve. You will continue this approach with the teams involved: simplify processes, automate repetitive work and keep human attention where it matters.

Managers remain responsible for their hiring decisions and teams. You will guide them, challenge them when necessary and agree priorities with the founders as recruitment and employee needs evolve.

What we offer

  • Compensation discussed in the first conversation, based on the scope and level of the role rather than your current salary.

  • Equity participation, through BSPCE where applicable.

  • Remote work from France or Germany, with flexibility around team commitments.

  • An annual company offsite.

  • Equipment, conference and training budgets, with time to learn.

  • Direct access to the founders and the opportunity to build a function that grows with the company.

How we hire

  1. 45 minutes with Emmanuel and Ludovic: the role, your experience and your questions.

  2. 60 minutes on your work: a hiring process you ran end to end and a complex international People situation you resolved.

  3. 45 minutes with two future colleagues: one from the commercial team and one from the technical team.

Three conversations, no take-home exercise, and a decision within two weeks of the first call.

Send your CV or LinkedIn profile.
